'''Geneviève Comte-Bellot''' (born 29 July 1929) is a French [[physicist]] specialising in [[fluid dynamics]]. She is known for her work on [[turbulence]] and [[aeroacoustics]].

== Biography ==
Comte-Bellot was born on 29 July 1929.<ref name="AT">{{cite web|url=https://www.academie-technologies.fr/members/118-genevi%C3%A8ve-comte-bellot|title=Geneviève Comte-Bellot|publisher=[[French Academy of Technologies]]|accessdate=14 October 2018|language=French|archive-date=15 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181015042203/https://www.academie-technologies.fr/members/118-genevi%C3%A8ve-comte-bellot|url-status=dead}}</ref> After obtaining her diploma from the [[Université Grenoble Alpes]] in 1953, she earned her [[master's degree]] at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] in Paris the following year.<ref name="APS">{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/units/dfd/awards/recipient.cfm?first_nm=Genevieve&last_nm=Comte-Bellot&year=2014|title=Recipient: Genevieve Comte-Bellot|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|year=2014|accessdate=14 October 2018}}</ref> She taught at a high school in [[Chalon-sur-Saône]] from 1954 to 1956, before joining the [[centre national de la recherche scientifique|French National Center for Scientific Research]] as a Senior Research Associate; Comte-Bellot remained in this position until 1967.<ref name="AT" /> In 1963, Comte-Bellot completed her dissertation "''Turbulent Flow between two parallel walls''", and was awarded a PhD by the Université Grenoble Alpes.<ref name="APS" /> She became a [[postdoctoral researcher]] and joined [[Stanley Corrsin]]'s team at [[Johns Hopkins University]] as a [[Fulbright scholar]] in 1963, where she oversaw his "Velvet wind-tunnel".<ref name="AT" /><ref name="APS" />

Comte-Bellot joined the [[École centrale de Lyon]] (ECL) in 1967 as a [[Academic ranks in France|Maître de Conférences]] (lecturer) and became a professor in 1971, before her promotion to Professeur de Classe exceptionnelle in 1982.<ref name="AT" /> At this university, she began researching [[aeroacoustics]]<ref name="APS" /> and founded the acoustics department in 1980. She served as director of the training and research unit (UER) of mechanics at [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1]] from 1977 to 1982.<ref name="AT" /> On 2 April 1990, Comte-Bellot was appointed as a corresponding member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-C/genevieve-comte-bellot.html|title=Geneviève Comte-Bellot|publisher=[[French Academy of Sciences]]|accessdate=14 October 2018|language=French}}</ref> Following her retirement, she became emeritus professor at the ECL in 1998.<ref name="AT" />

In 2005, Comte-Bellot was appointed as a Foreign Associate of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions in fluid mechanics and acoustics.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.nae.edu/File.aspx?id=7297|title=Celebrating Manufacturing Technology|page=47|journal=The Bridge|publisher=[[National Academy of Engineering]]|date=Spring 2005|accessdate=14 October 2018|volume=35|number=1}}<!--p49 of pdf--></ref>  She is also a member of the [[French Academy of Technologies]].<ref name="APS" />

She was appointed Commander of the [[Legion of Honour]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ec-lyon.fr/actualites/2013/genevieve-comte-bellot-commandeur-legion-honneur|publisher=[[École centrale de Lyon]]|date=21 February 2013|title=Geneviève Comte-Bellot commandeur de la Légion d'honneur|language=French|accessdate=14 October 2018}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The [[American Physical Society]] awarded her with their [[Fluid Dynamics Prize (APS)|Fluid Dynamics Prize]] in 2014.<ref name="APS" />
